name: Bio Medica Laboratories Limited
summary: Compliance and related-group capital allocation warrant a governance override. Parent sales are flat and cash conversion negative; IPO funds are not unrestricted surplus. Conditional parent-only model is diagnostic, not a consolidated fair-value recommendation.

sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text: Injectable-drug manufacturer with high reported margins but flat standalone sales, negative cash conversion and an unresolved production-license history. Acquisition and proposed sale of a subsidiary within a year complicate consolidated growth. Do not underwrite a pharmaceutical quality premium without the Unit-1 regulatory closure and disposal economics. [S1][S2]

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text: Manufactures parenteral medicines, including ampoules and vials. Unit-2 carries production after Unit-1 suspension. FY25 reported ampoule utilization 60.21% and vial utilization 71.73%; prospectus notes practical ceilings around 70% and 80% because of changeovers. Installed-capacity percentages must therefore be interpreted against practical rather than theoretical throughput. [S2]

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text: Sterile manufacturing know-how and approvals can form barriers, but regulatory compliance is a prerequisite, not proof of a moat. The prospectus identifies Unit-1 production suspension and concentrated customer revenues. No independently verified pricing power or durable contract advantage is established. [S2]

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text:
FY26 standalone revenue ₹38.2966 crore versus ₹38.3197 crore, essentially flat. Standalone PAT ₹11.6695 crore versus ₹9.7041 crore rose 20.25%, reflecting margin rather than revenue expansion. Consolidated revenue ₹43.0899 crore includes Vitamax; group PAT ₹11.8874 crore and owners’ profit ₹11.7806 crore must not be mixed. FY25 revenue reclassification is reconciled below; the remaining PAT/tax presentation difference is retained separately. [S1][S2]

Restated FY23/FY24/FY25 parent revenue was ₹16.2282/15.2494/38.1952 crore, PAT ₹0.3335/2.4987/9.7949 crore and CFO ₹2.2931/1.6241/−3.6717 crore. FY24 original PAT ₹2.6314 crore was reduced by ₹0.1327 crore in restatement through tax, gratuity and insurance adjustments; FY23 ₹0.3599 became ₹0.3335 crore. Current FY25 comparative revenue ₹38.3197 plus other income ₹0.0053 equals ₹38.325 crore total, matching prospectus ₹38.1952 plus ₹0.1298. Thus the revenue difference is reclassification, not missing sales. PBT ₹13.1427 crore agrees. Comparative PAT ₹9.7041 differs from restated ₹9.7949 crore with changed tax presentation. Printed tax lines also contain sign/arithmetic ambiguity, so the histories remain separate. Signed notes, rather than generic narrative, establish Indian GAAP. [S1] [S2]

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text: Vitamax was acquired on 25 September 2025. Board approved sale of the entire 51% holding on 27 July 2026, with shareholder approval on 27 August. Annual report gives Vitamax revenue ₹6.2471 crore and loss ₹0.2699 crore. Disposal completion, consideration, counterparty and recovery of intercompany funding remain open. New objects permit essential oils and botanical products; that authority is not evidence of an established profitable business. [S1]

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text:
The prospectus describes Unit-1 suspension after critical/major inspection findings and an unmet response deadline. Current revocation was not located; Unit-2 is distinct. The51% Vitamax subsidiary has promoter-owned49% minority and deep historical negative net worth. Shareholders authorized sale but buyer and price remain unspecified; enabling50cr RPT authority is not proof of actual transactions or misconduct.  [S1] [S2] [S4]

Vitamax Healthcare FY25 net worth −₹12.5014 crore and PAT −₹2.7004 crore preceded the 51% acquisition. Promoters Pradeep Mehta (25%) and Mukesh Mehta (24%) own the remainder. Parent investment cost ₹0.0051 crore is the share cost, not total exposure to subsidiary debts and goodwill. Annual parent notes show Vitamax advance ₹1.5546 crore plus loan ₹0.125 crore, totaling ₹1.6796 crore and explaining the governance advance figure. CARO nil principal after ₹2.5049 crore loan flows should not automatically be equated with every interest/advance balance. Borrowings from directors at FY26 close were ₹3.3429 crore from Mukesh and ₹3.8745 crore from Pradeep, with interest ₹0.2319/0.2309 crore; remuneration was ₹0.24 crore each. These disclosed transactions do not prove diversion. Disposal recovery and recourse remain unresolved. [S1] [S2] [S4]

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text:
Standalone FY26 CFO -₹5.7739 crore versus FY25 annual comparative -₹4.5742 crore; two-year CFO/PAT approximately -0.484x. FY26 inventory absorbed ₹15.1676 crore and receivables ₹4.9704 crore. PPE purchases ₹0.8816 crore give FCF proxy -₹6.6555 crore before subsidy ₹0.581 crore. Closing cash ₹0.0264 crore is pre-IPO. FY25 restated prospectus CFO -₹3.6717 crore differs from annual comparative; interest and tax classification differ, so do not splice those histories. [S1][S2][S3]

Parent FY26 core EBIT = 15.6941 + 1.8981 − 0.1339 = ₹17.4583 crore; FY25 = 13.1427 + 1.1951 − 0.0053 = ₹14.3325 crore. Assumed 25% tax gives NOPAT ₹13.0937/10.7494 crore. Equity + debt − cash capital of ₹49.2674/29.7406 crore gives average return 33.15%, but incremental return only 12.0%. Subsidy-adjusted PPE and expanding stock weaken interpretation of high reported ROCE. Group FY26 CFO is −₹6.0346 crore; tangible purchases ₹3.009 crore give FCF −₹9.0436 crore before asset sales/subsidy. Group cash ₹0.1035 and debt ₹39.9893 crore compare with parent cash ₹0.0264 and debt ₹22.8913 crore. Group goodwill ₹6.7135 crore and negative minority interest ₹6.174 crore cannot be ignored in a parent-only model. Printed group cash change is −₹11.23 lakh versus closing-minus-opening +₹8.52 lakh; acquisition effects need a bridge. Reported A/B/C totals sum to −₹10.74 lakh, a further subtotal discrepancy. [S1]

FY26 group PAT ₹11.8874 crore less parent PAT ₹11.6695 crore equals ₹0.2179 crore. The ₹0.1068 crore NCI allocation is approximately 49% of that difference, consistent with a post-acquisition profit contribution; the subsidiary’s full-year AOC loss ₹0.2699 crore is therefore not directly comparable. This resolves an apparent scope conflict, not the missing acquisition cash/goodwill bridge. Group loan note lists ₹6.75 crore unsecured funding from related party Prajal Nutrifoods alongside director/relative loans. Group leverage should not be replaced by the smaller parent-only figure. Positive audit/IFC reporting is retained as contrary evidence rather than omitted because the financial tables need correction. [S1]

Consolidated receivables note reports ₹9.8365 crore less than six months overdue, ₹0.7199 crore six-to-twelve months and ₹0.2968 crore two-to-three years, all classified good, with no doubtful allowance. Subsequent collections were not independently verified. Consolidated note32 identifies Prajal Nutrifoods as a sister concern. Its generic no-CWIP statement conflicts with ₹0.1975 crore CWIP on the group balance sheet, and the entity net-assets allocation table is not reconciled to the main balance sheet. These presentation/scope weaknesses reinforce G2; they do not establish theft or fictitious balances. Reasonable gap-resolution attempts included primary annual/result/prospectus cross-checks, the transaction notice/vote, current announcement cache and a search for later regulatory closure; no correcting primary filing or completed disposal terms were located. [S1] [S2] [S3] [S4] [S6]

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
Post-IPO12,575,001 shares and19October155.50 close imply195.5413cr market capitalization; FY26 parentPAT11.6695cr implies16.76× historical diluted-share earnings, not a forward multiple. Closing parent/group debt differs sharply and disposal remains conditional. Parent-only diagnostic scenarios are attached with explicit ring-fencing assumptions; they are not actual group fair value. [S1] [S2] [S90]

Official NSE observation: 2026-10-19 close ₹155.5, board lot 1000, turnover ₹4528600.0, 16.0 trades. This is a dated observation, not a current executable quote. Conditional 20/60-session statistics are attached under liquidity; missing-session and listing-history checks are still open. [S90]

Headline gross proceeds ₹52.4308 crore include OFS ₹5.2403 crore. Issuer fresh proceeds ₹47.1905 crore less stated expenses ₹5.1405 crore leave ₹42.05 crore, subject to actual expense allocation. Objects reconcile: debt ₹6.5 crore + plant ₹28.5 crore + general purposes ₹7.05 crore = ₹42.05 crore. The table labeled net ₹47.2903 crore deducts expenses but still includes OFS; it is not issuer free cash. The diagnostic model assumes March cash ₹0.0264 + issuer proceeds ₹42.05 − debt payment ₹6.5 = ₹35.5764 crore cash, and debt ₹22.8913 − ₹6.5 = ₹16.3913 crore. These are pro forma assumptions, NOT a verified October balance. Plant spending ₹28.5 crore is included over the first two model periods rather than counted simultaneously as surplus cash and free capacity. [S2]

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text:
A license problem at the remaining active production unit, customer loss or inventory impairment could hit both earnings and financing capacity. FY25 top customer represented 31.56% and top ten 75.11%, up from 8.06% and 53.95% in FY24. Subsidiary disposal may fail to recover capital or simplify the business as expected. [S1][S2]

Parent-only bear/base/bull terminal prices ₹72.14/227.52/450.14 imply conditional five-year CAGRs −14.24%/+7.91%/+23.69% at ₹155.50. Corresponding 15%-hurdle entry sensitivities are ₹35.87/113.12/223.80, and 18% FCFF cross-checks ₹40.37/108.39/208.97. These are NOT consolidated targets. All scenarios spend ₹28.5 crore plant capital and link annual NWC, capex, cash, debt, interest and tax. None needs additional debt above the assumed starting ₹16.3913 crore, but this does not prove actual funding: group recourse and interim use are unknown. A 20% parent inventory write-off is ₹6.6611 crore, 57.08% of FY26 parent PAT; a 30-day collection delay costs ₹3.1477 crore. Loss of subsidiary advances and investment adds ₹1.6847 crore. A severe sensitivity assigning all ₹17.098 crore group-minus-parent debt to the parent reduces terminal equity by ₹13.60 per share before interest, not a claim of actual legal recourse. A 20% plant overrun costs ₹5.7 crore. [S1] [S2] [S90]

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text:
Not supportable on the present evidence. Flat parent sales, negative cash conversion and post-IPO dilution make even the completed conditional earnings/cash bridge insufficient to establish a credible high-return target.

The prospectus compares Zenotech and Shukra but explicitly says they are not strictly comparable. FY25 parent EBITDA margin 39.83% compares with 45.28% and 39.06%; margins alone therefore do not establish a premium. The 8 May price/EPS/PE columns are date/corporate-action sensitive and not usable current multiples. At ₹155.50 a 15% five-year hurdle requires approximately ₹312.77 terminal price; at an assumed 15× PE on 12.575001 million shares that requires ₹26.22 crore PAT versus the ₹11.6695 crore parent baseline, plus cash conversion and capex. Five- and tenfold price gains require 37.97% and 58.49% annual returns. Governance, compliance and funding must work before that arithmetic becomes plausible. [S2] [S90]

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text: Obtain FDA suspension closure or current status; Unit-2 approvals and inspection records; disposal completion and related counterparty terms; inventory ageing and subsequent sales; customer retention; post-IPO deployment, debt repayment and fully diluted shares. Do not count a future disposal as completed. [S1][S2]

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text: Avoid — governance, subject to the dated source evidence and stated qualifications. Full research also retains a group financial-reliability hold. This classification follows the framework’s GOV3 override, not a finding of fraud or a declaration that a pending allegation is proven.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text: Prospectus history, restatement, customers, practical capacity, peers, litigation and subsidiary ownership reviewed; scanned current parent/group statements and audit controls visually checked. Post-listing transaction authority reviewed. Current disposal completion, group cash reconciliation and regulatory closure remain genuinely unresolved after source checks. [S1] [S2] [S3] [S4] [S5] [S6]

GOV.reason: Substantiated operational-compliance lapse and acquisition of a deeply negative-networth business with promoter minority exposure, followed quickly by unspecified disposal authority, warrant a low governance assessment. Contrary: issuer disclosed these facts and audited controls are positive. Pending personal allegations are NOT used as proof of guilt or as the score basis.

MOAT.reason: Sterile manufacturing capability has barriers, but Unit-1 regulatory history and concentrated customers weaken durability of advantage. High margins alone are not proof of pricing power.

REV.reason: FY25 growth followed a low base but FY26 parent sales are flat; group scope expansion is not organic growth. Customer concentration limits quality despite pharmaceutical demand.

DUR.reason: Injectable demand and funded capacity plans support an ordinary runway, constrained by compliance, practical utilization ceilings and concentration. Regulatory weakness is known risk rather than absence of all durability evidence.

CAP.reason: Average historical returns are high, but incremental standalone capital return is around12% versus a reasoned14–18% SME hurdle range and subsidiary allocation is unproven. IPO capacity is immature, not automatically worthless.

CASH.reason: Two full-year operating deficits with escalating inventory and an additional group cash reconciliation issue indicate persistent weak realization; positive FY23–24 cash is contrary evidence, not a cure for recent deterioration.

BAL.reason: IPO cash can strengthen the parent but is committed to plant/debt and group debt is substantially above parent debt. Inventory liquidity and disposal recourse matter; no default asserted.

EXEC.reason: Strong earlier profit growth is offset by flat current parent sales, unresolved old-unit compliance and rapid acquisition/divestment reversal. Capacity completion is not independently established.

EARN.reason: Audited profit is substantial but tax/comparative presentation, weak cash realization and group-scope inconsistencies reduce confidence. Other income is not the main profit driver.

ranking_eligibility.reason: Governance override and material group cash/scope uncertainty exclude investable/quality ranking even though conservative quality arithmetic is displayed.
